summary: Frontend-only Playwright testing of SYMSTRUO 15-slide investor pitch deck. All 20 test checks passed: cover content (SYMSTRUO wordmark, Rs 20L pill, DHANUSH B founder), sequential nav via next/prev buttons with correct disabled states on slide 1 and 15, keyboard ArrowLeft/ArrowRight navigation, overview grid open/thumbnail-jump/close, ?slide=9 deep-link to Competition, Ecosystem tab switching (all 5 modules), HowItWorks step buttons (0-4), Financials scenario toggles (Conservative/Base/Growth) changing chart content, UseOfCapital donut chart + Rs 20L center label rendered, Vision Express Interest modal with empty-form error toast, success toast + auto-close on valid submit, and modal-close button.

issues: Recharts logs many 'width(0)/height(0)' warnings when slides mount/unmount via AnimatePresence (charts briefly render at 0-size before ResponsiveContainer measures). Purely console noise — no visual defect — but could be silenced by conditionally rendering charts only after mount, or using explicit min-height.

critical_code_review_comments: Deck.jsx line 119: Space key ' ' is bound to next-slide navigation globally, which will also fire when focus is on a button (buttons accept Space to activate) — currently mitigated by e.preventDefault after the button click already handled, but could cause double-advance in edge cases. Consider ignoring keys when e.target is a BUTTON/INPUT/TEXTAREA.

Recharts ResponsiveContainer inside AnimatePresence-exiting slide emits width/height 0 warnings on every slide transition. Non-blocking but noisy. Consider setting explicit width/height on the LineChart or gating render on visibility.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 15 slides render correctly. All data-testid selectors from the review request exist and are wired up. Express Interest form is mocked (toast only, no persistence) as expected. Recharts console warnings are cosmetic. If revisiting, viewport 1920x1080 works; also worth spot-checking print/PDF export via window.print() which is available on data-testid=export-pdf-button but was not exercised.
